subject: Follow-up: Token volumes & batching assumptions
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elliot John <elliot.john@finpay.com>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sun, 28 Mar 2027 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up: Token volumes & batching assumptions

Hi Elliot —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap and the two asks we discussed:

1) Volume & cadence: you mentioned ~10M tokens/day on weekdays with a heavy tail during batch processing windows (end-of-day reconciliation) and ~4M tokens/day on weekends. You also said peak concurrency for real-time requests is typically 40-60 concurrent sessions.

2) Workload mix: ~70% short-turn chat (avg 120 tokens/request) and ~30% longer generation (avg 1,800 tokens/request) for report generation. Continuous streaming for chat is important to your UX.

Next steps I promised: a simple token-level unit economics sketch at a $/1M token granularity, and assumptions for continuous batching and concurrency that would meet your latency targets (~200-300ms p50 for chat, tail SLAs on long generations). I've attached a short spreadsheet with the math and a draft proposal.

High-level notes from the calc:
- Baseline unit price target: $X per 1M tokens (see attachment) - want to confirm your budget range so we can align on a target $/1M tokens that makes sense.
- Continuous batching: with your steady cadence and the mix above, we expect sustained batching efficiency (continuous batching) to reduce per-token GPU cost by ~20-30% versus naive single-request execution, assuming a small prefix cache and 500-800ms batching windows for chat.
- Concurrency: for 60 concurrent chat sessions with streaming, plan capacity for steady-state plus a 2x burst headroom. Our Dedicated offering can reserve that capacity to keep p50/p90 in-target while saving on overprovisioning.

Could you confirm:
A) Target budget band for token spend (monthly) - e.g., $/month or target $/1M tokens?
B) Any hard latency constraints beyond the p50 number above?

I'll follow up with a quick call invite for a 30-minute scoping session with one of our Solutions Engineers (Camila) so we can map runtimes, batching windows, and a pilot plan.

Regards,

Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com
Attachment: pricing_token_breakdown.xlsx (spreadsheet)
Attachment: proposal_finpay_03-2027.pdf (PDF)

From: Elliot John <elliot.john@finpay.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 29 Mar 2027 08:09:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Token volumes & batching assumptions

Thanks Marissa - this is helpful. A couple clarifications from our side:

- Budget: we’re evaluating a pilot budget of $15k- $25k/mo to start, with the intent to scale to ~$80k- $120k/mo if the pilot shows the expected cost/performance. If helpful, think of an initial target of ~$20k/mo.
- For the $/1M tokens target, our finance team prefers a target below $350 per 1M tokens for the pilot phase.
- Latency: for chat the p50 target is 200-250ms; p95 should be under 600ms for production. For report generation, we can tolerate 2-4s p50, but the p95 should be <8s.

A few workload details: our peak batch window (reconciliation) runs from 02:00-05:00 UTC, where you’ll see a spike of long generations (the 1,800 token type). We want to avoid heavy cold-starts during that window.

Samantha (cc’d) will own procurement and contract terms on our side.

-Elliot

On Sun, Mar 28, 2027 at 3:02 PM Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com> wrote:
> [quoted above]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elliot John <elliot.john@finpay.com>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwoodinference.com>, Samantha Li <samantha.li@finpay.com>
Date: Mon, 29 Mar 2027 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Token volumes & batching assumptions

Elliot - thanks, that budget band is really helpful and the $/1M target gives us a clear optimization goal. A few follow-ups and assumptions I want to call out explicitly before the scoping call:

1) Pricing sketch: the attachment includes a modeled target of $300 per 1M tokens for the pilot (within your <$350 target) that assumes:
   - Continuous batching delivering ~25% token-cost reduction (mix-weighted)
   - 95% prefix reuse for short-turn chat (we'll validate with a small sampling run)
   - Quantization/instance selection optimizations for the long-generation model paths

2) Batching & windows: for chat we recommend a continuous batching window of 400-700ms to keep p50 in the 200-300ms range while capturing aggregation benefits. For the reconciliation job (long runs), we recommend using reserved Dedicated capacity to run those windows on pre-warmed instances with sustained throughput - this avoids cold-start penalties during the 02:00-05:00 UTC spike.

3) Concurrency planning: to meet your p95 targets under load, our rough capacity plan is: steady-state capacity for 60 concurrent chat sessions + reserved headroom for 2x burst for sudden spikes. For long runs, plan for an autoscaling profile that maintains baseline throughput and ramps over a defined period to handle the 02:00-05:00 window.

4) Pilot design & metrics: we'll run a 30-day pilot focused on verifying per-token unit cost, p50/p95 latency, and batching efficiency (measured as effective tokens per GPU-second). That will give us the real numbers to finalize a committed Dedicated plan.

Can you confirm the pilot budget (we used $20k/mo in the draft) and whether procurement needs any specific contractual language (SLA, data residency, KMS)? Once confirmed, I'll send a calendar invite for Wed or Thu and loop in Camila for technical scoping.

Best,

Marissa

Attachment: pricing_token_breakdown.xlsx (revised)
